newsitem.title: USA: Citizens to take $185 mln Q2 charge.
newsitem.headline: Citizens to take $185 mln Q2 charge.

text.p: Citizens Utilities Co said Thursday its restructuring the company will lead to a $185 million charge and lower earnings in the second quarter.

"Because of lower-than-expected long distance and adjacent market revenues and the charge, Citizens earnings per share (with and without the charge) for the second quarter ... will decline more than they did in the first quarter of this year," said treasurer Robert DeSantis in a statement.

Citizens posted a net of $30.2 million, or $0.13 a share, in the first quarter. This marked a 22 percent decline from the first quarter in 1996 when the company posted a net of $38.9 million, or $0.16 a share.
A May 1 First Call consensus put the company's second-quarter earnings at $0.13 a share, compared with $0.20 a share in the 1996 quarter.
Citizens said it will take a $185 million pre-tax charge in the second quarter and reduce its 1997 capital expenditure program by at least $175 million to account for the restructuring.

The company said it expects the restructuring to reduce operating expenses by at least $70 million annually. Citizens said the measures include cutting its work force and benefits, consolidating call centers, closing sales offices, and reducing slaes and marketing activities.
DeSantis said the $185 million charge in the secon quarter related to the costs of cutting the workforce, ending leases, and changing informartion systems and software.
He added recent Federal Communication Commission orders relating to access charge reform have made the company reconsider its rural telephone investment program.

The company on April 30 already warned its 1997 and 1998 earnings would be below 1996 levels because of accelerated expenses and planned capital expenditures in those years. Citizens' stock closed at 8-15/16 Thursday, close to its 52-week low of 8-11/16.
